title: Physical scale ruler
question: Where does a labeled length, time, or mass sit on an International System of Units (SI) logarithmic ruler, and what is its evidence status?
predictionPrompt: Choose one family and a matching labeled scale, predict its base-10 exponent, then inspect whether the entry is defined, derived, measured, or illustrative.
sourceRevision: PHYSICS_TOUR_MASTER_PLAN.md, 2026-07-26 contract; BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment; IAU 2012 Resolution B2; IAU 2015 Resolution B3
sourceLocator: Chapter 4 scale-ruler contract; fixed SI constants; CODATA Planck scales; IAU 2012 astronomical-unit definition; exact declared or derived Julian-year, light-year, and parsec relationships; IAU 2015 nominal solar conversion constant
caveats: Defined, derived, measured, and order-of-magnitude illustrative catalog statuses are not interchangeable.
A normalized logarithmic coordinate compares stated magnitudes and does not predict a scale.

modelComponents.label: SI logarithmic coordinate
modelComponents.description: Maps each positive same-family SI quantity value to a dimensionless base-10 logarithmic coordinate relative to one stated SI unit.

attribution.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; tour-scale-ruler-v1 contract
caveats: Changing the reference unit shifts the coordinate and creates no physical prediction.

assumptions: Every selected catalog value is finite, positive, and interpreted only within its declared length, time, or mass family.
The selected preset belongs to the selected quantityFamily; invalid cross-family pairs fail rather than being coerced.
Planck-scale SI values use exact hbar and c with measured G and therefore inherit uncertainty from G.
Representative entries are pedagogical scales and catalog proximity carries no causal meaning.

The astronomical unit is exact under IAU 2012 Resolution B2; the Julian year is declared as 365.25 days, the light-year is derived from c times that interval, and the parsec is derived geometrically as 648000/pi astronomical units.
Exact IAU nominal solar and planetary values are conversion constants and are not exact measurements of the corresponding bodies.
No empirical dataset is fitted or compared.
